 Parents, rejoice: 'KPop Demon Hunters' is coming to Indianapolis. Tickets, dates:
 Heather Bushman, Indianapolis Star Updated Fri, November 13, 2026 at 3:30 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Parents, rejoice: 'KPop Demon Hunters' is coming to Indianapolis. Tickets, dates: If you spent weeks on end looping "Golden" or scoured the shelves for a purple braided wig during Halloween, you might have a chance to make your kids' whole year: "KPop Demon Hunters" is coming to Indianapolis.
 HUNTR/X, the movie's fictional band that sells out stadiums and banishes baddies back to the shadow realm, will come to life at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on June 23, 2027, as part of a massive Golden World Tour. The concert, which will hit nearly 50 cities worldwide, promises a "first-of-its-kind" production that uses animations, stunts, choreography and audience participation to immerse fans in the "Kpop Demon Hunters" experience.
 The event promises "a next-generation K-pop concert experience unlike anything fans have seen, heard, or felt before," according to a news release.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Tickets for the Golden World Tour's Indianapolis stop go on sale Nov. 20, and more information is available at kpopdemonhunterstour.com . Presale begins at 10 a.m. Nov. 19, and registration is also available on the tour's website .
 "KPop Demon Hunters" hits the road on the heels of an unbelievably dominant year. The record-smashing animated feature is Netflix's most popular film ever , and the accompanying soundtrack's inescapable hit "Golden" nabbed a Grammy and an Oscar and shot to the top of the Billboard Hot 100 for eight weeks last year.
 As a girl group, HUNTR/X doesn't just live inside the screen. Real recording artists Ejae, Audrey Nuna (who headlined Fountain Square's Chreece hip-hop festival last year) and Rei Ami comprise the band in the studio and on stage, and they've logged performances at the Academy Awards and the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade. The Golden World Tour, though, will stick with the characters Rumi, Mira and Zoe as its headliners.
